Consider the following statements:
1. Jhelum River passes through Wular Lake.
2. Krishna River directly feeds Kolleru Lake.
3. Meandering of Gandak River formed Kanwar Lake.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: Statement 1 is correct: Jhelum originates from a spring at Verinag in J&K, located at the foot of the Pir Panjal Range. It is called Vyeth in Kashmiri, Vetesta in Sanskrit, and Hydaspes in Greek. It is the main waterway of the Kashmir Valley, which flows through Srinagar and Wular Lake. This transboundary river joins the Chenab near Jhang in Pakistan. Statement 2 is incorrect: Kolleru Lake was once a lagoon, but it is now several kilometres inland due to coastline emergence and delta formation. The lake is fed directly by the seasonal Budameru and Tammileru streams and is connected to the Krishna and Godavari systems via several inflowing drains and channels (it is not directly fed by the Krishna River). It was declared a Ramsar site in 2002 for its ecological importance. Statement 3 is incorrect: Kanwar Lake, also known locally as Kabartal, is located in Bihar's Begusarai district. It is a residual oxbow lake and Asia's largest freshwater oxbow lake. It is formed due to the meandering of the Burhi Gandak River, a tributary of the Ganga. It is a rain-fed lake, according to waterbody experts, and fills up during Indian Geography PMF IAS Geo – 76 the monsoon season. Challenges faced by Kanwar Lake: Increasing silt accumulation, deforestation, and land disputes.

Godavari river originates at Trimbakeshwar in Nasik district Maharashtra. It travels 1465 km and empties into the Bay of Bengal. It has seen a revival in the Kanha National Park and Tiger Reserve (KNPTR) after near-extinction. Successful breeding programs and conservation efforts helped in the species' recovery at KNPTR. Swamp deer are extinct in Pakistan and Bangladesh, now found only in southwestern Nepal and central/northeastern India. There are three subspecies of swamp deer in the Indian Subcontinent:  Western swamp deer (Rucervus duvaucelii) found in Nepal.  Southern swamp deer (Rucervus duvaucelii branderi) found in central and north India.  Eastern swamp deer (Rucervus duvaucelii ranjitsinhi) found in Kaziranga and Dudhwa National Parks.

Consider the following pairs:

2. Loktak Lake Barail Range
3. Namdapha National Park Dafla Hills
Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
41.x: Pair 1 is correct: Nokrek Biosphere Reserve is located in northeast India, on the Tura Range, which forms part of the Meghalaya Plateau (average altitude: 600 metres). The entire area is mountainous, and Nokrek is the highest peak of the Garo hills, rising up 1,412 metres. Vegetation: Evergreen, semi-evergreen & deciduous. Pair 2 is incorrect: Loktak Lake is a freshwater lake in Manipur. It is the largest freshwater lake in the northeastern region. Keibul Lamjao, the only floating national park in the world, floats over it. Thick, floating mats of weeds covered with soil (phumids) are a characteristic feature. It is not located in the Barail Range. The Barail Range is the highest hill range in Assam and serves as the watershed separating the Brahmaputra and Barak river systems. Pair 3 is incorrect: It is located in Arunachal Pradesh between the Dapha Bum range of the Mishmi Hills and the Patkai range. It is crossed by the Noa Dihing River (a tributary of the Brahmaputra River) that originates at Chaukan Pass. It is the largest protected area in the Eastern Himalaya biodiversity hotspot. It is the only park in the World to have the four Feline species of big cat, namely: Tiger, Leopard, Snow Leopard and Clouded Leopard. It is famous for the critically endangered Namdapha flying squirrel, which is endemic to the park. Vegetation: Evergreen to temperate broadleaf forest. • Daphla (or Dafla) Hills is a tract of hilly country on the border of western Arunachal and Assam.

It is maintained as part of the Ramsar list. 14. Which of the following helps some hydrophytes to thrive in wetlands and marshes where water level fluctuates time to time ? (a) Rhizomatous roots (b) Submergent roots (c) Aerenchyma tissue (d) Rhizophores Uttrakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2024 Ans-(c) Hydrophytes are adapted to living in aquatic environment. They are found in wetland and marshy areas. This adaptation in these plants is due to the presence of 'Aerenchyma' tissue. This tissue creates spaces or air channels in the leaves, stems and roots of the plants. These air channels provide buoyancy to aquatic plants, allowing them to float. The channels of air filled cavities provide a low-resistance internal pathway for the exchange of gases such as oxygen, carbon dioxide and ethylene between the plant above the water and the submerged tissues.

43.s: Contour bunding is a method of soil conservation used in

43.x: Contour bunding is a method of soil conservation primarily used in hilly and sloping terrain, where runoff can cause significant soil erosion. In this technique, small embankments are constructed along contour lines to slow down the flow of water, thereby reducing soil loss and improving moisture retention. It is not suitable for desert margins, where wind erosion is dominant; nor for low, flat plains prone to flooding, where drainage measures are more relevant; nor for scrublands dealing with weed spread. 3. Zero tillage In the context of global climate change, which of the above helps/help in carbon sequestration/storage in the soil?
43.x: Any method which helps the soil to retain more organic matter so that it may work as an effective Carbon sink would be helpful in Carbon sequestration or storage. Contour bunding is one of the extensively used soil and water conservation technique in several rainfed areas. Contour bunding is a Mechanical measure which minimizes the soil erosion. Relay cropping means that a new crop is planted or sown before the previous one is harvested. This can provide advantages for both crops as one of them may provide nitrogen, shade, support or may discourage pests. The obvious benefit of Relay cropping is soil conservation. Zero tillage is also based on the premise of soil conservation, the basic premise is to minimize the disturbances to the soil leading to an increase in retention of water, nutrients and topsoil itself. Zero tillage has carbon sequestration potential through storage of soil organic matter in the soil of crop fields. Thus all the three help in carbon sequestration.

3. Avoiding the cultivation of plantation crops.
4. Using crop residues to cover soil surface
5. Adopting spatial and temporal crop sequencing/ crop rotations.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
43.x: Conservation agriculture is a method that keep agricultural cost low. High profits and sustainable product can be brought. Along with this, there is a balanced increase in natural resources like soil, water, environment, and biological factors. In this, there is a balanced and proper use of agricultural chemicals and inorganic and organic sources along with agricultural activities such as zero tillage/minimum tillage, so that there is no adverse effect on the various bio-functions of agriculture. In conservation agriculture, minimum tillage allows crop residues to remain on the soil surface. This greatly reduces soil erosion. Generally it is very important to keep the soil covered by crop residues up to 30 percent. It is very important to adopt crop diversification and crop rotation in protected cultivation.Generally, farmers follow the same type of crop rotation for many years. For example, farmers have been planting the paddy wheat cropping system in the same field for years, which directly affected the fertility of the soil. It does impact crop diversification maintains soil fertility and reduces crop related pests and diseases.

Statement 4 is incorrect: REEs are a set of 17 elements, not 13. They are also included in India's list of 30 critical minerals. PMF Concept Hack: Statement 4 can be eliminated first using basic understanding. The term critical minerals includes minerals that are strategically important for modern technologies, and Rare Earth Elements are among the most discussed critical minerals globally. So saying REEs are not included in critical minerals is unlikely. Once Statement 4 is eliminated, only options (a) and (b) remain. At this stage, you do not even need to worry much about Statement 3. 44.s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Statement I: In India, State Governments have no power for making rules for grant of concessions in respect of extraction of minor minerals even though such minerals are located in their territories.
2. Statement II: In India, the Central Government has the power to notify minor minerals under the relevant law. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
44.x: Statement I is incorrect: Section 15 of the MMDR Act empowers the State Governments to make rules for regulating the grant of quarry leases, mining leases or other mineral concessions in respect of minor minerals and for purposes connected therewith. Hence, the regulation of minor minerals comes under the legislative and administrative domain of the State Governments. Further, Section 23C of the MMDR Act empowers the State Governments to make rules for preventing the illegal mining, transportation, and storage of minerals, and for purposes connected therewith. Hence, control of illegal mining comes under the legislative and administrative purview of the State Governments. Statement II is correct: The central government has the power to notify "minor minerals" under section 3 (e) of the MMDR Act, 1957.

44.s:
Consider the following minerals:

2. Chromite
3. Kyanite
4. Sillimanite In India, which of the above is/are officially designated as major minerals?
44.x: Bentonite is incorrect: A mineral is a naturally occurring substance characterized by unique chemical and physical properties, composition, and atomic structure. In India, minerals are classified as major or minor under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2015, to assess output value in the mining and quarrying sector. As per Government of India official notification released in 2015 Bentonite (locally known as multani mitti or Fuller's earth) has been declared as 'Minor Mineral'. Chromite is correct: Chromite is a major mineral. It is a dark grey, metallic, oxide mineral often mistaken for magnetite due to its metallic lustre and occasional magnetic properties. It can be found in basic igneous rocks, as well as in metamorphic and sedimentary rocks formed from weather-affected chromite-bearing rocks. It is a crucial metal used to make hard, tough, and chemically resistant steel. The chromium extracted from chromite is used in chrome plating and alloying to produce corrosion-resistant superalloys, nichrome, and stainless steel. More than 96% of chromite resources are located in Odisha (Jajpur, Kendujhar, and Dhenkanal). Kyanite is correct: Kyanite is a major mineral. It occurs in metamorphic aluminous rocks. It has high-temperature resilience. Its quality relies on aluminium content: more aluminium, higher grade. It is primarily used in metallurgical, ceramic, glass, and cement industries. It is also used to make spark plugs in automobiles. Jhark

44.x: Statement 1 is correct: In India, monazite has been the principal source of rare earths. It occurs in association with other heavy minerals, such as ilmenite, rutile, zircon, etc., in the beach sands and inland placer deposits. Statement 2 is correct: It also contains thorium and uranium. Statement 3 is incorrect: Although India possesses large deposits of monazite, they are not found in all coastal sands. Monazite is found in the coastal tracts of Cuttack and Ganjam districts of Odisha. In Andhra Pradesh, thick ilmenite and monazite placers are found around Vishakapatnam and Bhimunipatnam. The beach sands in Kerala and Tamil Nadu are also very rich in monazite. Approximately 7.23 million tonne Rare Earth Oxides (REO) Equivalent contained in 13.15 million tonne monazite resource, occurring in the coastal beach and teri / red sand in parts of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat and in the inland alluvium in parts of Jharkhand, West Bengal and Tamil Nadu. Statement 4 is correct: Indian Rare Earths Limited (IREL), a wholly owned Public Sector Undertaking of the Government of India (GOI) under the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), is the only entity which has been permitted to produce and process monazite and handle it for domestic use as well as for export. 47.x: Nallamalai Hills are situated between the Krishna River and Pennar River, stretched from north to south, parallel to the Coromandel Coast on the Bay of Bengal. Javadi Hills are located on the Eastern Ghats in the Vellore and Tiruvannamalai districts of Tamil Nadu State. Renowned as the ‘Blue Mountains’, Nilgiri Hills are located at the junction of Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats. Doddabetta is the highest peak in the Nilgiri Hills at 2,637 metres. The Anaimalai or Anamalai Hills form the southern portion of the Western Ghats and span up to the border of Kerala and Tamil Nadu in southern India. Anaimudi is the highest peak in the Anaimalai Hills at 2695 metres. These four hills are located in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Kerala states in India from north to south. 48.s: Who among the following rulers of Vijayanagara Empire constructed a large dam across Tungabhadra River and canalcum-aqueduct several a kilometres long from the river to the capital city?
48.x: Deva Raya I (c. 1406–1422 CE) was a prominent ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire known for his contributions to irrigation, military organisation, and cultural patronage. He commissioned a massive dam across the Tungabhadra River along with a canal-cum-aqueduct system to supply water to the capital, and also constructed another dam on the Haridra River to support agriculture. The celebrated Hazara Rama Temple, a fine example of Deccan architecture, was built during his reign. His court was visited by travellers such as Nicolo Conti, who left valuable accounts of the empire. Deva Raya I strengthened the Vijayanagara army by improving cavalry forces, employing Turkic archers, and importing quality horses from Arabia and Persia. He was also a patron of Kannada literature and architecture, with the noted Jain poet Madhura associated with his court, a tradition that continued from his father Harihara II's time. Additional Information: The Vijayanagar kingdom constituted four dynasties — Sangama (c.1336–1485 CE), Saluva (c.1485–1503 CE), Tuluva (c.1503–1570 CE) and Aravidu (till the end of the 17 th century). Harihara and Bukka (c.1336–1377 CE) were founders of the Sangama dynasty of the Vijayanagar kingdom. Mallikarjuna, Vira Vijaya, and Virupaksha were rulers of the Sangama Dynasty, but historical records are unclear about their exact timelines, and their rule saw no significant accomplishments.

48.s: Telugu Ganga Canal Water is supplied to which of the following states?
48.x:
The Telugu Ganga Project is an inter-state water project designed primarily to supply drinking water to Chennai (Tamil Nadu) while also providing irrigation benefits to Andhra Pradesh. The project utilizes surplus waters of the Krishna River and conveys them through a network of reservoirs and canals. Water flows through Srisailam Reservoir, Somasila Reservoir, Kandaleru Reservoir, and finally reaches Poondi Reservoir near Chennai. Apart from supplying drinking water to Chennai, the project also provides irrigation facilities to drought-prone districts of Rayalaseema and parts of Nellore district. The project is an example of interstate cooperation involving Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. However, the state receiving drinking water under the project is Tamil Nadu. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).

• Major Reservoirs – Srisailam, Somasila, Kandaleru

48.s:
Consider the following statements :
1. Jhelum River passes through Wular Lake.
2. Krishna River directly feeds Kolleru Lake.
3. Meandering of Gandak River formed Kanwar Lake.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Wular's main source of water is Jhelum river. There is a small island in the centre of this lake, called 'Zaina Lank'. It is worth mentioning that this island was constructed by King Zainul-Abi-Din. Hence statement 1 is correct. While talking about second statement, Kolleru lake does not directly feed the Kolleru lake but the lake is fed by two other rivers namely Budameru and Tammileru. These two rivers are connected to the Krishna and Godavari systems by inflowing drains and channels. Hence we can say that the Krishna River indirectly feeds the Kolleru lake through its tributaries. Therefore, statement 2 is not correct. The meandering of the Gandak river did not form the Kanwar Lake, that is a freshwater oxbow lake located in Begusarai District of Bihar, India. The Godavari basin extends over Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha, as well as smaller parts of Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Puducherry. The Godavari basin is the second-largest basin in India.The River rises from Trimbakeshwar in the Nashik district of Maharashtra. It is the largest peninsular Indian river that drains into the Bay of Bengal. It divides into two main streams, the Gautami Godavari on the east and the Vashishta Godavari on the west and forms a large delta before it pours into the Bay of Bengal. The delta of the Godavari is lobate, with a rounded bulge and numerous distributaries. • Important cities: Nashik, Paithan, Nizamabad, Rajahmundry, etc., • Right bank tributaries: Pravara, Manjira, and Maner. • Left bank tributaries: Purna, Pranahita, Indravathi, and Sabari Indian Geography PMF IAS Geo – 83 • Indravati River: It flows through the states of Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh in India. It originates in the Eastern Ghats in the Kalahandi district of Odisha and flows for a distance of 535 kilometres before joining the Godavari River at Bhadrachalam in Telangana. • Pranahita: It flows through the states of Maharashtra, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh in India. 49.s: India gets maximum rainfall mainly from –
49.x: During April and May, when the Sun shines between the equator and the Tropic of Cancer (Northern Hemisphere), the large land mass in the north of Indian Ocean gets intensely heated. This causes the formation of intense low pressure in the northwestern part of the subcontinent followed by the northward shift in the position of Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ). The south-west monsoon may thus, be seen as the continuation of the southeast trades deflected towards the Indian subcontinent after crossing the equator. The Southwest monsoon enters India in two rain-bearing systems. The first originates in the Bay of Bengal causing rainfall over the plains of north India. second is the Arabian Sea current of the south-west monsoon which brings rain to the west coast of India. According to data provided by India Meteorological Department for the year 2024, The southwest monsoon supplies almost the entire rainfall.

51.s: Among the following Tiger Reserves, which one has the largest area under "Critical Tiger Habitat"?

The Krishna River flows through the reserve, while both the Srisailam Reservoir and Nagarjunasagar Reservoir lie within its boundaries. • Vegetation: tropical dry mixed deciduous forest. • Major Fauna: Bengal tiger (EN), leopard, Indian pangolin (EN), spotted deer (chital) (LC), sambar (VU), blackbuck, chinkara, four-horned antelope (chausingha) (VU), mugger (marsh crocodile) (VU), etc.

52.s: In India, the largest soil group is found as :
52.x: Alluvial soil is the largest and most important soil group in India. Covering about 15 lakh sq. km or about 45.6% of the total land area of the country, these soils contribute the largest share of our agricultural wealth. The widest occurrence of the Alluvial soils is in the Indo-Gangetic plain starting from Punjab in the West to West Bengal and Assam in the East. They are also found in deltas of Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Cauvery, where they are called deltaic alluvium. Along the coast, they are known as coastal alluvium. Some alluvial soils are found in Narmada and Tapi (Tapti) valleys. Geologically, the alluvium is divided into newer or younger Khadar and older Bhangar soils. Geographically, Black soils are spread over 5.46 lakh sq. km while the red soils occupy a vast area of about 3.5 lakh sq. km.

Consider the following statements:

52.x: Soils in tropical rainforests are generally poor in nutrients. Intense and continuous rainfall leads to leaching, where soluble nutrients are washed away from the topsoil, preventing their accumulation. The high temperature and humidity in tropical rainforests accelerate the decomposition of organic matter. Microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi rapidly break down dead plants and animals, releasing nutrients. Although nutrients are released quickly, they are immediately absorbed by dense vegetation or lost through leaching. As a result, the soil itself does not become nutrient-rich.

52.s: Laterite soils are predominant in:
52.x: Laterite soil is found in typical monsoon conditions such as high temperature and heavy rainfall with wet and dry periods. The alterations of the wet and dry seasons leads to the leaching away of siliceous matter and lime from the rocks, leaving behind a soil rich in oxides of iron and aluminum compounds. These are leached soils of wet humid tropical regions, which are less fertile. They are well developed in parts of Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, South Maharashtra, parts of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal, Kerala, Jharkhand, Assam and Meghalaya. Laterite soils are widely spread in India and cover an area of 2.48 lakh sq km. Laterite soil is mostly spread in Kerala (Malabar coastal region) followed by Maharashtra. (c) 'Black Soil' or 'Regur Soil' or 'Black Cotton Soil' is generally clayey, deep and impermeable. It swells and becomes sticky when wet, and shrinks when dried. 53.s: Which is the oldest basin in Andhra Pradesh?
53.x:
The Kadapa Basin (Cuddapah Basin) is the oldest geological basin in Andhra Pradesh and one of the oldest sedimentary basins in India. It was formed during the Proterozoic Era, approximately 1.6 billion years ago, and consists of thick sequences of sedimentary and metamorphic rocks. The basin occupies large parts of YSR Kadapa, Nandyal, Kurnool, Annamayya and Prakasam districts. The Kadapa Basin is economically important because it contains rich deposits of limestone, barytes, asbestos, dolomite, quartz and uranium. The famous Mangampeta Barytes Mine, one of the largest barytes deposits in the world, is located within this basin. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:

• Famous Mineral – Barytes (Mangampeta)

Rainfall *Generally in India rainfall occurs from the month of June to September when south-west monsoon is effective throughout the country. In this period, the low-pressure zone of North- Western India is very intense and systematic. Due to low air pressure, south-east winds from the tropic of Capricorn in the Southern Hemisphere cross the equator and are attracted towards the Indian Peninsula. Passing over the oceans these winds are filled with humidity and split into two branches - Arabian Sea branch and Bay of Bengal branch. *When the south-west monsoon winds enter the terrestrial area, it rains with an intense thundering and torrential storms. The arrival of these winds and rainfall is called ‘burst’ of the monsoon. *The speed of these winds is about 30 km/h on average and they become effective throughout the country within a month. *According to the data Rainfall Statistics of India (2024), almost the entire rainfall is received from the southwest monsoon (June-September). *Monsoon winds of the Arabian Sea are obstructed by the Western Ghats. These winds climb the slope of the Western Ghats and soon become cool causing heavy rainfall on the windward side of Western Ghats. These winds cause little rainfall to the east of the Western Ghats. The region of low rainfall is known as the rain-shadow area

56.x: Japan, Italy, and South Korea are frequently mentioned in the media for their low birth rates: countries such as Japan, Italy, and South Korea are facing challenges related to low birth rates, ageing populations, or overall population decline. In Italy, the average number of children per woman fell from 1.24 in 2022 to 1.2 in 2023, as per government data. Experts warn that if the current demographic trend persists, Italy's population — currently around 59 million — could shrink by nearly 1 million by 2030. Japan reported a decline in births for the eighth consecutive year in 2023, setting yet another record low. In South Korea, government figures indicate an 8% drop in the fertility rate in 2023 compared to the previous year. (South Korea's birthrate rose in 2024 for the first time in nine years). Additional Information: What is the 'fertility rate' and how different it's from 'birth rate'? Both fertility rate and birth rate are indicators of population growth, but they are not the same. The fertility rate indicates the average number of children a woman of childbearing age is expected to have; a fertility rate of 2.1 is considered the "replacement rate." On the other hand, the birth rate measures the number of live births per 1,000 people in a given population each year. Minimum: **two rooms**, **two teachers**, **teaching aids**.

61.s: Which of the following NEP 2020 stage – age group pairs is correctly matched?
61.x: NEP 2020 stages: Foundational 3–8, Preparatory 8–11, Middle 11–14 and Secondary 14–18 years.
xa: Stage lengths: **5** (Foundational), **3** (Preparatory), **3** (Middle), **4** (Secondary).
It means **12 years of school + 3 of pre-school**.

61.s: Samagra Shiksha (2018) subsumed which schemes?
o: RMSA, Saakshar Bharat and NIPUN Bharat
61.x: Samagra Shiksha covers pre-school to Class 12 and subsumes SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education.

61.s: NEP 2020 replaced the National Policy on Education, 1986 after how many years?
61.x: NEP 2020 replaced NPE 1986 after 34 years.

61.s: Mana Badi Nadu-Nedu provides how many basic facilities in schools?
61.x: Nadu-Nedu provides nine facilities, including toilets, drinking water, furniture and English labs.

61.s: Which state ranked first among the larger states in primary education in the Index on Foundational Literacy and Numeracy 2021?

Consider the following about gender indicators in education:
1. Female GER in higher education rose to 30.2.
2. Female GER exceeded male GER.
3. Gender parity was reported at all school levels.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
61.x: All three are correct: female higher-education GER reached 30.2, exceeded male GER, and gender parity was reported at all school levels.
xa: Source: MoSPI **Women and Men in India 2025** (**1 May 2026**).
NFHS-5: women with **10+ years** of schooling **41%**.

61.s: Which State recorded the highest FLN score in the second edition of the Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Index released for the EAC-PM?
61.x: Punjab recorded the highest FLN score in the second edition of the FLN Index.
61.tq: Use the ranking fact directly and avoid substituting a generally high-literacy State for the indexed State.
xs: **Punjab** had the highest FLN score in the second edition — option **(2)** (APPSC-GS 2022 key).
The **FLN Index** is by the **Institute for Competitiveness** for the **EAC-PM**.
xa: **NIPUN Bharat** targets Grade-3 FLN by **2026-27**.
NEP 2020 foundational stage: ages **3-8**.
61.fixed: stem cited an answer key; reworded (y84eb9277d15)

61.s: International Literacy Day is observed on:
61.x: International Literacy Day is observed on 8 September.
61.tq: Use the exact observance date and avoid confusing it with other education-related days.
xs: **International Literacy Day**: **8 September** — option **(3)**.
A **UNESCO** day since **1966**, first observed in **1967**.
xa: **Saakshar Bharat** was launched on ILD **2009**.
ILD **8 Sep 2026** theme: "**Literacy for people, the planet and prosperity**".
⚠ **14 November** = Nadu-Nedu launch date (2019).

61.s: As per UDISE+ 2024-25, the dropout rate at the secondary level was:
61.x: Secondary dropout fell to 8.2% from 10.9%; 3.5% and 2.3% are the middle and preparatory rates.

61.s: As per AISHE 2023-24, the female GER in higher education was:
61.x: AISHE 2023-24 gives female GER 31.2 with GPI 1.08; overall GER was about 30.

61.s: As per NFHS-5, the share of women with 10 or more years of schooling was:
61.x: NFHS-5 shows 41% (NFHS-4: 35.7%); 71.5% is women's literacy.

61.s: International Literacy Day was first observed in:
61.x: UNESCO declared it in 1966 and it was first observed in 1967.

62.s: In the Census, a main worker is one who worked for at least ____ in the reference year.
62.x: A main worker worked 183 days (six months) or more in the reference year.
xa: Census 2011: main workers **75.2%**, marginal **24.8%** of all workers.
Four categories: **cultivators**, **agricultural labourers**, **household industry**, **other workers**.
⚠ PLFS **UPSS** counts as employed anyone who worked **30+ days** in the year.

62.s: For a Census Town, at least what share of male main workers must be in non-agricultural activities?
62.x: A Census Town needs 5,000+ population, 75%+ of male main workers in non-agricultural work and density of at least 400 per sq km.
xa: Criteria **unchanged since 1981**; retained for **Census 2027** (**17 Sep 2026**).
Census non-workers include **students**, **household duties**, **dependants**, **pensioners**, **rentiers**.

62.s: Which of the following is NOT a Census category of non-workers?
62.x: The Census categories include students, household-duty persons, dependants, pensioners, rentiers, beggars or vagrants and others. Permanent industrial employers are not listed as a category.
62.tq: Identify the outsider in a classification list.
xs: **Permanent industrial employers** are not a non-worker category — option **(1)**.
Census non-workers: **students**, **household duties**, **dependants**, **pensioners**, **rentiers**, **beggars/vagrants**, others.
xa: Worker categories: **cultivators**, **agricultural labourers**, **household industry**, **other workers**.

62.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Cultivator — Works on another person's land for wages
Agricultural labourer — Cultivates only government land
Household industry worker — Production within the household
Other worker — Works exclusively in agriculture
62.x: A household industry worker is engaged in production within the household, such as handloom work. A cultivator works on own or leased land, while an agricultural labourer works on another person's land for wages.
62.tq: Match each occupational label with its precise defining activity.
xs: **Household industry worker — production within the household** (e.g. **handloom**) — option **(3)**.
A **cultivator** cultivates **own or leased land**; working on **another person's land for wages** = **agricultural labourer**.
**Other workers** do **non-farm** work — factory, trade, transport, services, government.
xa: Household industry = **3.8%** of India's workers (2011).
Main worker: **183+ days**; marginal: less.

62.s: In the Census, a person working on another's land for wages is classified as a(n):
62.x: Agricultural labourers work on another's land for wages; cultivators work own or leased land.

62.s: In the Census, a person cultivating leased land is classified as a(n):
62.x: Cultivators work on own or leased land.

62.s: A Census Town must have a population density of at least:
62.x: A Census Town needs 5,000+ population, 75%+ male main workers non-farm and 400+ per sq km.

62.s: What is the shortest distance between Stall-3 he tha and Stall-6?
The percentage of labour force in agriculture in 2011-12 has changed from 56.70 percent in 2001 to
62.x: The share of the workforce in agriculture declined from 56.7% (2001) to about 48.9% (2011-12).

62.s: Which of the following Statements is not true
o: according to the 2011 census, 48.9 Per cent of main workers of labour force were employed in agricultural and allied sectors
the proportion of workers in 2011-12 employed in the services sector is 36.7 Per cent
the relative size of the services sector grew during the period 1991-2011
there has been a marked difference in the occupational structure of different categories

62.s: As per Census 2011, which category formed the largest share of India's workers?
62.x: Other workers formed 41.6% of workers, ahead of agricultural labourers (30.0%), cultivators (24.6%) and household industry workers (3.8%).
xa: ⚠ In 2011, **labourers outnumbered cultivators** for the **first time**.
Agriculture's share of workers: **58.2% (2001)** → **54.6% (2011)**.

62.s: According to the 2011 Census, which category first exceeded the other in India?
62.x: In 2011, agricultural labourers constituted 30.0% of workers, exceeding cultivators at 24.6% for the first time.
62.tq: Direct comparison of two closely related occupational categories.
xs: In **2011**, **agricultural labourers exceeded cultivators** for the **first time** — option **(4)**.
Labourers **30.0%** vs cultivators **24.6%**.
xa: ⚠ **2001**: cultivators **31.7%** > labourers **26.5%**.
Women workers: **55%** agricultural labourers vs **24%** cultivators.

62.s: In Census 2011, marginal workers formed about ____ of India's total workers.
62.x: Of 4,818.89 lakh workers, main workers were 75.2% and marginal workers 24.8%.
xa: Marginal workers: **1,193.23 lakh**.
Non-workers: **7,288.27 lakh** (about **60%** of population).

62.s: The share of agriculture in India’s workforce declined from 2001 to 2011 from:
62.x: Agriculture’s share of workers declined from 58.2% in 2001 to 54.6% in 2011, while the secondary and tertiary shares increased.
62.tq: Read the direction of change carefully and reject the reversed sequence.
xs: Agriculture's share of workers fell **58.2% (2001)** → **54.6% (2011)** — option **(2)**.
**Secondary and tertiary** shares rose.
xa: **NSS 2011-12**: agriculture about **48.9%** of workers.
**PLFS Q2 FY26**: agriculture **42.4%** of employment.

62.s: In rural India, Scheduled Castes are concentrated mostly among:
62.x: Scheduled Castes are largely marginal farmers and landless agricultural labourers.
xa: High agricultural-labourer states: **Bihar, AP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha**.
Agricultural labourer = works on **another person's land for wages**.

62.s: The overall Work Participation Rate of India in Census 2011 was:
62.x: The overall WPR was 39.8% (male 53.3%, female 25.5%); about 60% were non-workers.
xa: Workers: **4,818.89 lakh** — main **75.2%**, marginal **24.8%**.
Main worker = worked at least **183 days**; marginal = less than **183 days**.
2011: **agricultural labourers (30.0%)** outnumbered **cultivators (24.6%)** for the first time.
AP's Census 2011 WPR: about **46.6%** — above India.

62.s: Which of the following pairs (worker category – share of India's workers, Census 2011) is correctly matched?
62.x: Other workers were 41.6%; agricultural labourers 30.0%, cultivators 24.6% and household industry 3.8%.

62.s: In Census 2011, the male and female Work Participation Rates of India were, respectively:
62.x: Male WPR was 53.3% and female 25.5%; 39.8% was the overall WPR.

62.s: In Census 2001, cultivators and agricultural labourers formed, respectively, what share of India's workers?
62.x: In 2001 cultivators (31.7%) exceeded labourers (26.5%); in 2011 it reversed (24.6% vs 30.0%).

62.s: In 2011-12, services employed about ____ of India's workers.
62.x: Services employed about 27% in 2011-12; the 36.7% claim is not true (APPSC-G2 2017).

62.s: In Census 2011, about what share of India's population were non-workers?
62.x: With WPR at 39.8%, about 60% of the population were non-workers.

62.s: Census 2011 counted India's total workers as:
62.x: India had 4,818.89 lakh workers in 2011: 75.2% main and 24.8% marginal.

62.s: Which of the following groups is correctly associated with a high cultivator share among workers?
62.x: Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland are identified with a high cultivator share. Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry have high shares of other workers.
62.tq: Use the occupational-category distinction to avoid confusing cultivator-heavy and other-worker-heavy regions.
xs: High **cultivator** share: **Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland** — option **(2)**.
**Delhi, Chandigarh, Puducherry** have high "**other workers**"; **Bihar, AP** have high **agricultural-labourer** shares.
xa: High agricultural labourers: **Bihar, AP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha**, Jharkhand, West Bengal, MP.
**HP** also has a high **WPR**.

62.s:
Consider the following statements about Work Participation Rate (WPR):
1. WPR tends to be higher in several less-developed, hill and tribal states.
2. Subsistence activities in such regions often require greater dependence on manual labour.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
62.x: Both are correct; the greater need for manual labour in subsistence activities explains the higher WPR in these states.

62.s: Which group of States/UTs has a high share of 'other workers'?
o: Jharkhand, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh
62.x: Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry have high other workers; Himachal and Nagaland have high cultivators.

62.s: By Census 2011 pattern, Andhra Pradesh belongs to the group of States with a high share of:
62.x: AP is among the States with high agricultural labourers, with Bihar, Chhattisgarh and Odisha.

62.s: Under Current Weekly Status, a person is counted as employed if he or she worked for at least ____ on any day of the reference week.
62.x: CWS counts one hour of work on any day of the reference week as employment.
xa: ⚠ The **1-hour CWS rule** may hide distress and underemployment.
**WPR** = employed / **total population** x 100.

62.s: The U-curve of female labour force participation is associated with:
62.x: Claudia Goldin's U-curve says women's work participation first falls and then rises with development; India followed the declining half till 2018-19.
xa: Reasons for the rise: **unpaid family work**, **distress**, **COVID return migration**, broader **survey coverage**.

62.s: Under UPSS, a person is counted as employed if he or she worked for at least ____ in the year.
62.x: UPSS counts 30 or more days of work in the 365-day reference year as employment.
xa: **CWS**: 7-day week; employed if worked at least **1 hour** on any one day.
CWS captures **short-term / seasonal** unemployment.
⚠ UR denominator = **labour force**; PU and WPR denominator = **population**.
PLFS is run by the **NSO (MoSPI)**.

62.s: Which one of the following is the correct expression for the Worker Population Ratio (WPR)?
o: Labour force divided by total population multiplied by 100
Employed persons divided by total population multiplied by 100
Unemployed persons divided by labour force multiplied by 100
Unemployed persons divided by total population multiplied by 100
62.x: WPR equals employed persons divided by total population, multiplied by 100.
62.tq: Focus on the denominator to distinguish WPR from LFPR and unemployment rate.
xs: **WPR = employed persons / total population x 100** — option **(2)** (RPSC 2024 key).
(Employed + unemployed)/population = **LFPR**; unemployed/labour force = **UR**; unemployed/population = **PU**.
xa: ⚠ UR denominator = **labour force**; PU and WPR = **population**.

62.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey is conducted by the:
o: NITI Aayog under the Ministry of Finance
Registrar General of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs
Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Rural Development
62.x: The PLFS is conducted by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
62.tq: Use the institution-authority association to reject swapped departmental options.
xs: PLFS is run by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under **MoSPI** — option **(1)**.
It gives **LFPR**, **WPR**, **UR** and **PU** indicators.
xa: Headline rates for age **15+**.
"Working age" varies: **15-59**, **15-64** or **16-64** — check the stem.
Status measures: **usual status**, **UPSS**, **CWS**, **CDS**.

62.s: In PLFS, the unemployment rate is calculated with ____ as the denominator.
62.x: UR = unemployed / labour force; WPR uses total population as the denominator.

62.s: In PLFS, the Labour Force Participation Rate is:
62.x: LFPR counts employed plus unemployed against population; employed / population is WPR.

62.s: According to the Claudia Goldin U-curve, India was on the falling half of female labour participation till:
62.x: India was on the falling half of the U-curve till 2018-19.

62.s: The reasons for low productivity in Indian agriculture is-
62.x: Overcrowding in agriculture, small land holding and traditional agricultural practices all three are among the main reasons for low productivity in Indian agriculture. 25. Assertion (A) : Green Revolution Technology played a crucial role in gradually transforming traditional agriculture into a modern scientific one. Reason (R) : It did not involve much of social and environmental costs. Select the correct answer from the codes given below: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). (b) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). (c) (A) is true, but (R) is false (d) (A) is false, but (R) is true U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2014 Ans. (b) Green Revolution Technology played a crucial role in gradually transforming traditional agriculture into modern scientific agriculture with the use of irrigation, specialized seeds, fertilizers, pesticides and machinery. So, Assertion (A) is true. Green Revolution does not involve social and environmental cost. Its success was due to a combination of high rates of investment in crop research, infrastructure, etc. The environmental cost is widely recognised as a potential threat for long term sustainability. Thus, (R) is also true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

62.s: In Q2 of FY 2025–26 (July–September 2025), agriculture's share of total employment in India was:
62.x: Agriculture had 42.4% of employment, self-employment 55.8% and casual labour 18.9%.
xa: Rural jobs **57%** agricultural; urban jobs **62%** in services.
**56.2 crore** employed (15+); **8.7 lakh** jobs added over Q1 (ES 2025-26).

62.s: Which of the following correctly gives the annual PLFS 2025 values for LFPR, WPR and UR, respectively?
62.x: The annual PLFS 2025 figures were 59% for LFPR, 57% for WPR and approximately 3% for unemployment rate.
62.tq: Preserve the order of the three indicators while matching the annual release figures.
xa: Youth UR: **9.9%**.

62.s: For January–March 2026 under CWS for persons aged 15 years and above, which combination is correct?
62.x: For January–March 2026, the CWS estimates were LFPR 55.5%, WPR 52.8% and UR 5.0%.
62.tq: Match the release period and survey status before comparing the figures.
xs: **59 / 57 / 3** are annual PLFS 2025.
xa: Urban UR **6.6%**, rural **4.3%**.
Female LFPR **34.7%**.

62.s: A fall in the unemployment rate may not signal better jobs because it may reflect:
62.x: A lower unemployment rate may reflect distress entry into low-productivity work rather than creation of decent, secure employment.
xa: The **1-hour CWS rule** may hide underemployment.
Jan-Mar 2026 UR: **5.0%**; annual PLFS 2025: **3%**.

62.s: The one-hour Current Weekly Status rule may conceal which of the following?
o: Only long-term unemployment among urban graduates
The statutory duration of MGNREGA employment
The exact size of the organised workforce
Underemployment and inadequate utilisation of labour
62.x: The one-hour CWS criterion can classify a person as employed even when work is insufficient, thereby hiding underemployment.
62.tq: Apply the measurement concept to a short employment scenario and identify what the indicator may miss.
xs: The **1-hour CWS rule** may hide **underemployment** and **distress** — option **(4)**.
Anyone who worked **1 hour on any day** of the week counts as employed.
xa: Rising **unpaid family work** may also mask distress.
⚠ A fall in UR may reflect **distress entry** into low-productivity work.

62.s: In Q2 of FY 2025-26, self-employment accounted for about ____ of total employment.
62.x: Self-employment was 55.8%; agriculture 42.4% and casual labour 18.9%.

62.s: Which factor has contributed to the increasing feminisation of farm work in India?
o: A rise in women’s share of operational holdings to 55%
62.x: Men’s out-migration has increased women’s participation in farm work, even though women hold only 12.8% of operational holdings.
62.tq: Link the stated demographic movement with its occupational consequence.
xs: **Men's out-migration** drives the **feminisation of farm work** — option **(3)**.
Women hold only **12.8%** of operational holdings, not 55%.
**Mechanisation** cut manual demand, and **unpaid family work** has risen — options **(2)** and **(4)** fail.
xa: Women workers (2011): **55%** agricultural labourers.
Mechanisation cut manual demand (**2004-05 to 2012**).

62.s: In Census 2011, women formed about ____ of India's agricultural labourers.
62.x: Women were 55% of agricultural labourers but only 24% of cultivators, and held 12.8% of operational holdings.
xa: **Men's out-migration** → **feminisation** of farm work (UPSC).
Rural women gave **80%** of the rise in female workers (2017-18 to 2023-24).
62.fixed: 55%/24% are shares of women workers by category, not women's share of all labourers/cultivators (women are ~43% of agri labourers)

62.s: India's female LFPR (aged 15 and above) in 2017–18 was:
xa: Rural women gave **80%** of the rise.
Rural gains led by **West Bengal, UP, Bihar**.

62.s: Which of the following is identified as a reason for the rise in female work participation in India?
o: Universal availability of flexible working hours
62.x: Broader survey coverage is a stated reason for the rise, along with subsistence farming, unpaid family work, distress and return migration; flexible hours are not available universally.

62.s: Which of the following has contributed to low female work participation in India?
o: Mechanisation reducing demand for manual labour
Wide availability of flexible working hours
62.x: Mechanisation, greater education of girls, lack of flexible hours, distance, safety concerns and family duties have lowered female work participation.
xa: ⚠ **Subsistence farming** explains the **rise**, not low levels.
Women hold only **12.8%** of operational holdings.

62.s: India's female LFPR (aged 15+) in 2022-23 was about:
In Census 2011, women held only about ____ of operational holdings.
62.x: Women held only 12.8% of holdings, though they were 55% of agricultural labourers.

62.s: Which of the following is NOT cited as a reason for low female work participation in India?
62.x: MGNREGS work raised rural female WPR; mechanisation, schooling of girls and safety are reasons for low levels.

62.s: According to the 2011 census, which district of Andhra Pradesh has the highest share of cultivators in the total main workers?
According to Census 2011, the largest share of all workers in Andhra Pradesh was engaged as:
62.x: Agricultural labourers formed 47.9% of all workers in Andhra Pradesh, followed by other workers at 34.8%.
62.tq: Identify the maximum value in the state-wise occupational share comparison.
xs: **Agricultural labourers** were AP's largest group: **47.9%** of all workers — option **(4)**.
**Other workers 34.8%**, **cultivators 14.5%**, **household industry 2.9%**.
xa: All agricultural labourers: **110.52 lakh** (**86.12** main + **24.40** marginal).
⚠ India's largest group is **other workers (41.6%)**.

62.s:
Consider the following statements about the Census 2011 Work Participation Rate of Andhra Pradesh:
1. Calculated from 230.81 lakh workers out of 495.77 lakh population, it was about 46.6%.
2. It was lower than the all-India rate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
62.x: 230.81 / 495.77 gives about 46.6%, which is higher than the all-India rate, so statement 2 is wrong.

62.s: As per PLFS 2023–24 (usual status, all ages), the LFPR of Andhra Pradesh was:
62.x: AP's LFPR was 47.5% and WPR 45.6%, above India's 45.1% and 43.7%.
xa: AP female LFPR **35.8%** vs India **31.7%**.
AP LFPR rural **50.1%**, urban **41.3%**.

62.s: Which was cited as one reason for the higher female work participation rate in rural Andhra Pradesh?
62.x: MGNREGS was cited as one reason for the higher female work participation rate in rural areas.
xa: **MGNREGA**: Act **2005**; launched **2 Feb 2006** at **Bandlapalli, Anantapur (AP)**.
Up to **100 days** of wage work per rural household per year.

62.s: As per PLFS 2023-24, the female LFPR of Andhra Pradesh is:
62.x: AP's female LFPR is 35.8%, above India's 31.7%, yet urban young women (15-29) have a WPR of only 15.9%.
xa: AP female WPR: **39.6% rural** vs **22.8% urban** (PLFS 2023-24).
**MGNREGS** is one reason for higher rural female WPR.

62.s: In 2011, main agricultural labourers formed about ____ of Andhra Pradesh's main workers.
62.x: AP had 86.12 lakh main agricultural labourers out of 193.17 lakh main workers, about 45%.
xa: AP = **4.79%** of India's total workers.
AP main cultivators: **30.93 lakh** (~**16.0%**).

62.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh had the highest share of agricultural labourers?
62.x: West Godavari had the highest share of agricultural labourers; Chittoor had the most cultivators.

62.s: As per PLFS 2023-24, the WPR of Andhra Pradesh was:
62.x: AP's WPR was 45.6% (LFPR 47.5%); India's WPR was 43.7%.

62.s: In Census 2011, cultivators formed about ____ of Andhra Pradesh's workers.
62.x: AP's cultivators were 14.5%; agricultural labourers 47.9% and other workers 34.8%.

62.s: Andhra Pradesh's main agricultural labourers make up nearly ____ of India's main agricultural labourers.
62.x: AP's 86.12 lakh main agricultural labourers are nearly 1 in 10 of India's.

62.s: MGNREGA was launched on 2 February 2006 at which place?
62.x: MGNREGA was launched on 2 February 2006 at Bandlapalli in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh.
62.tq: Apply the who-where-when recall pattern to a flagship employment programme.
xs: MGNREGA was launched at **Bandlapalli, Anantapur** (AP) — option **(1)**.
So the national programme began in **Andhra Pradesh**, not Tirupati, Amaravati or Vijayawada.
xa: Guarantees up to **100 days** of wage work.
**MGNREGS** helps explain AP's higher **rural female WPR** (**39.6%**).

62.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: MGNREGA – Up to 100 days of wage work per rural household a year
PMEGP – Merger of PMRY and REGP
62.x: PMEGP's nodal agency is KVIC, not NABARD.
xa: ⚠ MGNREGA **Act 2005**, **launched 2006** — at **Bandlapalli (Anantapur)**, AP.
**NAPS (FY26)**: **6,100+** enterprises; **9.9 lakh** apprentices.
AP's poverty strategy cites **10 lakh+ SHGs**.

62.s: e-Shram, the database of unorganised workers, was launched on:
62.x: e-Shram was launched on 26 August 2021; 2 February 2006 was MGNREGA's launch.

62.s: Workers registered on e-Shram get a Universal Account Number of:
62.x: e-Shram gives a 12-digit UAN; 31.89 crore were registered by 18 August 2026.

62.s: The nodal agency for PMEGP is:
62.x: PMEGP's nodal agency is KVIC, not NABARD.

62.s: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, which replaced MGNREGA from 1 July 2026, guarantees:
62.x: VB-G RAM G guarantees 125 days, up from MGNREGA's 100 days.

63.s: The share of Scheduled castes in the Country's population in the year 2001 was:

66.x: Platyrrhine refers to a broad nose with a nasal index of 85 or above. Leptorrhine is below 70 and mesorrhine is 70–84.9.
66.tq: Apply the numerical boundary to the category instead of recalling labels alone.
xs: A nasal index of **86** is **Platyrrhine** (broad nose; **85 and above**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mesorrhine** = **70-84.9**; **Leptorrhine** = under **70**.
**Dolichocephalic** is a head-shape term, not a nasal one.
xa: **Risley** ranked castes mainly by the **nasal index**.
Risley's dictum: caste status varies **inversely** with nasal index.
⚠ **Risley** = nasal index; **Sarkar** = cephalic index; **Haddon** = hair form.

66.s: The cephalic index of a living person is 83. Under the standard classification, this head type is:
66.x: For a living head, a cephalic index of 82 and above is brachycephalic (round-headed), 77-81.99 is mesocephalic and 76.99 and below is dolichocephalic (long-headed), so 83 is brachycephalic. Platyrrhine is a nasal-index class (85 and above), not a head type.
66.tq: Living head CI: ≤76.99 dolicho, 77-81.99 meso, ≥82 brachy.
xs: A living CI of **83** is **Brachycephalic** (round; **82 and above**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Mesocephalic** = **77-81.99**; **Dolichocephalic** = **76.99** and below.
**Platyrrhine** is a nasal category.
xa: Dry skull: brachycephalic = **80 and above**.
Guha's **Western Brachycephals**: Alpinoid, Dinaric, Armenoid.
CI = (maximum breadth / maximum length) x **100**.

66.s: Which racial group is associated with straight, coarse hair described as leiotrichi?

xs: **Leiotrichi** (straight, coarse hair) is **Mongoloid** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Cymotrichi** (straight-wavy) = **Caucasoid**; **ulotrichi** (woolly) = **Negroid**.
xa: ⚠ **leio – cymo – ulo** = **straight – wavy – woolly**.
**Haddon (1924)** used **hair form** as the main basis for world populations.
Mongoloids have **sparse hair**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Recently, all the countries of the United Nations have adopted the first-ever compact for international migration, the 'Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM)'.
2. The objectives and commitments stated in the GCM are binding on the UN member countries.
3. The GCM addresses internal migration or internally displaced people also in its objectives and commitments.
How many of the above statements are correct?
69.x: All statements are incorrect: The Global Compact on Migration is the first-ever UN global agreement on a common approach to international migration in all its dimensions. On December 19, 2018, the United Nations General Assembly officially endorsed the compact through a vote, with 152 countries supporting the resolution (not all countries). It is of a non-legally binding nature. It is intended to: Address all aspects of international migration, including the humanitarian, developmental, human rights-related and other aspects;  Make an important contribution to global governance and enhance coordination on international migration;  Present a framework for comprehensive international cooperation on migrants and human mobility; International Relations PMF IAS Misc – 47  Set out a range of actionable commitments, means of implementation and a framework for follow-up and review among Member States regarding international migration in all its dimensions;  Be guided by the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the Addis Ababa Action Agenda; and  Be informed by the Declaration of the 2013 High-Level Dialogue on International Migration and Development. • The GCM is primarily focused on international migration and does not directly address internal migration or the situation of internally displaced persons. PMF Concept Hack: Statement 1 can be eliminated because the phrase "all the countries of the United Nations" is a classic UPSC trap. International agreements and compacts

69.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Recently, all the countries of the United Nations have adopted the first-ever compact for international migration, the ‘Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM)’.
2. The objectives and commitments stated in the GCM are binding on the UN member countries.
3. The GCM addresses internal migration or internally displaced people also in its objectives and commitments.
How many of the above statements are correct?
69.x: The Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration is the first intergovernmental agreement, adopted under the auspices of the United Nations, to cover all dimensions of international migration in a holistically and comprehensive manner. It was adopted at an intergovernmental conference on migration in Marrakesh, Morocco, on 10 December 2018. At the ceremony to adopt the text on 10 December, only 163 countries formally adopted it. Further, countries like Austria were critical of it and refrained from adopting it in 2018. Hence statement 1 is not correct. The Global Compact for Migration is the first-ever UN global agreement on a common approach to international migration in all its dimensions. The global compact is non-legally binding. Hence, statement 2 is not correct. The Global Compact enumerates 23 objectives for State action, bolstered by specific commitments, that seek to address challenges related to today’s migration. The GCM commitments and actions can be seen as a guide for States to meet their human rights obligations when designing migration governance measures to reduce the risks and vulnerabilities migrants face at different stages of migration and to create conducive conditions that empower all migrants to become active members of society. Key commitments include: Strengthening evidence-based and human rights-based policy-making and public discourse on migration; Minimizing the adverse drivers of migration, including combating poverty and discrimination

80.s: Which one of the following groups of plants was domesticated in the 'New World' and introduced into the 'Old World'?
80.x: After Christopher Columbus returned from his first voyage to the Caribbean in 1493, a significant event known as the Columbian Exchange began. The Columbian Exchange involved the transfer of goods, ideas, and resources between the Old World and the New World in the years following Columbus's expedition. The Old World refers to the Eastern Hemisphere, which includes present-day Europe, Africa, and Asia, while the New World refers to the Western Hemisphere, encompassing the Americas. This period of exchange was especially prominent during Modern Indian History PMF IAS IH – 61 the 1500s and 1600s. All three plants – tobacco, cocoa, and rubber – were domesticated in the Americas (the "New World") and were introduced to the Old World. PMF Concept Hack: This question does not require knowing the origin of every crop. An aspirant with basic awareness of geography and agriculture can solve it by identifying the odd one out in each option. In option (b), cotton is a red flag. In option (c), sugarcane is a clear red flag, and in option (d), wheat is an obvious red flag. Once these obvious mismatches are identified, options (b), (c), and (d) can be eliminated without knowing the origin of every plant. This leaves tobacco, cocoa, and rubber, which are all associated with the New World.

86.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

86.tq: Classify industries by weight change and location tendency.

**Bakery** is **market-based** (weight-gaining or fragile products, located near consumers).
**Iron and steel** is raw-material-based (about **4 t** of input per tonne), and **cement** is raw-material-based on **limestone** — neither is market-based or footloose.
xa: **Power-oriented**: **aluminium**, needing **14,000-15,000 kWh** per tonne.
**Footloose** examples: **software**, **electronics**, and **cotton textiles** (cotton is a "pure" material).
⚠ Both **sugar** and **iron & steel** are weight-losing, so Weber puts them near raw material (**MI > 1**).

86.s: Market-based industries are generally located near consumers because their products are:

**Weight-losing and perishable** inputs describe **raw-material-oriented** industries (sugar, iron & steel, cement), not market-based ones.
Dependence on cheap electricity is **power orientation** (aluminium).
xa: In Weber's theory, **MI < 1** or **ubiquitous inputs** (such as **water**) pull an industry **near the market**.
**Footloose** industries locate anywhere with **skills and links** — software, electronics, diamond polishing.
Location factors include **raw material**, **power**, **market**, **labour**, **transport**, water and **government policy**.

86.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Alfred Weber's least-cost theory?
o: A Material Index above 1 pulls the industry towards the market
A plant first locates where total transport cost is lowest, then adjusts for labour and agglomeration
A Material Index below 1, or ubiquitous inputs such as water, favours the market
86.x: MI above 1 (weight-losing inputs, e.g. iron and steel, sugar) pulls the plant to the raw material, not the market.
xa: **Pure raw material** (no weight loss, e.g. **cotton**) → free to locate anywhere.
**Footloose** = **software / diamond** (APPSC **2019**).
Steel needs about **4 t** of input per tonne.

86.s: In Weber's least-cost theory, a 'pure' raw material such as cotton, which loses no weight in processing, allows the industry to be located:
o: Anywhere between the source and the market
86.x: A pure raw material has no weight loss, so transport cost is the same whether raw material or product is moved; the plant is free to locate anywhere between source and market. Weight-losing inputs (MI > 1) pull it to the source (A); weight-gaining or ubiquitous inputs (MI < 1) pull it to the market (B); a port location (D) is not implied by the theory.
86.tq: Pure material (cotton) = free location; weight-losing = source; ubiquitous = market.
xs: A **pure raw material** such as **cotton** loses no weight, so the plant can locate **anywhere between the source and the market** — option **(3)**.
**Weight-losing** inputs (**MI > 1**) pull the plant to the raw-material source.
**MI < 1** or ubiquitous inputs (water) pull it to the market.
xa: This is why **cotton textiles** are listed as **footloose** in the orientation table.
**Alfred Weber (1909)**: least total transport cost first, then labour and agglomeration adjustments.
Iron & steel needs about **4 t** of input per tonne — a classic weight-losing case.

The project was launched in 2001 as part of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP). The East-West Corridor links Porbandar (Gujarat) in the west to Silchar (Assam) in the east. Statement 2 is incorrect: The India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway is a 1,360 km-long route under construction, connecting Moreh (Manipur), India, with Mae Sot, Thailand, via Myanmar. The IMT highway is part of India's Look East policy and aims to boost trade and commerce in the ASEAN–India Free Trade Area and Southeast Asia. India has proposed extending the highway to Cambodia, Laos, and Vietnam, forming the ~3,200 km East-West Economic Corridor. The E-W Economic Corridor between Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam became operational in 2015. Statement 3 is incorrect: The 2800 km BCIM corridor was proposed to link Kunming in China's Yunnan province with Kolkata, passing nodes such as Mandalay in Myanmar and Dhaka in Bangladesh before heading to Kolkata. China-Myanmar Economic Corridor (CMEC) is the newest of the six land corridors under the BRI, and has assumed prominence in place of the Bangladesh China India Myanmar (BCIM) corridor, which has largely stalled.

95.s: Which is the longest canal of commercial importance in Andhra?
95.x:
The Buckingham Canal is the longest navigation canal on the eastern coast of India and the most important canal of commercial significance in Andhra Pradesh. Constructed during the British period, the canal extends for about 796 km, running parallel to the Coromandel Coast from Andhra Pradesh to Tamil Nadu. It connected several important ports and facilitated the transport of rice, salt, timber, textiles and agricultural produce before the development of railways and highways. In Andhra Pradesh, the canal connected important centres such as Kakinada, Eluru, Machilipatnam and Nellore, making it a vital route for inland water transport. Although the K.C. Canal, Bandar Canal and Eluru Canal are important irrigation canals, they do not possess the same commercial and navigational significance as the Buckingham Canal. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Longest Navigation Canal – Buckingham Canal
• Length – Approximately 796 km
• Importance – Inland navigation and commercial transport

98.x: All four sites mentioned in the question are included in the UNESCO World Heritage List. The Champaner- Pavagadh Archaeological Park is recognised for its unique blend of Hindu and Islamic architectural traditions and its historical urban landscape. The Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus in Mumbai is an outstanding example of Victorian Gothic Revival architecture in India and continues to function as a major railway station. Mamallapuram (Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram) is known for its rock-cut temples, cave sanctuaries, and monumental open-air reliefs that reflect Pallava art. The Sun Temple at Konark is a classic example of Kalinga architecture, designed as a colossal chariot dedicated to the Sun God.

Initially built by Queen Udayamati in memory of her husband, King Bhima I of the Solanki dynasty, in the 11 th century. The stepwell was constructed as both a religious and functional structure and designed as an inverted temple, highlighting the sanctity of water. Rani-ki-Vav was built in the Maru-Gurjara architectural style. The property is protected as a national monument by provisions of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites Act of 1958. 99.s: Where was the first nuclear power station established in the world?
99.x: The pursuit of nuclear energy for electricity generation began soon after the discovery in the early 20th century that radioactive elements, such as radium, released an immense amount of energy, according to the principle of mass-energy equivalence. In 1932, James Chadwick discovered the neutron, which was immediately recognized as a potential tool for nuclear experimentation because of its lack of an electric charge. Experimentation with a bombardment of materials with neutrons led Frederic and Irene Juliut-Curie to discover induced radioactivity in 1934, which allowed the creation of radium-like elements at much less the price of natural radium. Further work by Enrico Fermi in the 1930s focused on using slow neutrons to increase the effectiveness of induced radioactivity. In the United States, where Fermi and Szilárd had both emigrated, this led to the creation of the first man-made reactor, known as Chicago Pile-1, which was successfully operated on December 2, 1942. This work became part of the Manhattan Project, which made enriched uranium and built large reactors to breed plutonium for use in the first nuclear weapons, which were used on the cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Electricity was generated for the first time by a nuclear reactor on December 20, 1951, at the EBR-I (Experimental Breeder Reactor-1) experimental station near Arco, Idaho,USA which initially produced about 100 kW.Thus, option (d) is the correct answer.
